label: Bible Study
prompt: I am _____ with Christ: nevertheless I live; yet not I, but Christ liveth in me: and the life which I now live in the flesh I live by the faith of the Son of God, who loved me, and gave himself for me.
verse: I am crucified with Christ: nevertheless I live; yet not I, but Christ liveth in me: and the life which I now live in the flesh I live by the faith of the Son of God, who loved me, and gave himself for me.
note: Paul's most personal summary of the gospel — 'who loved me' is singular on purpose.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: We love him, because he _____ loved us.
verse: We love him, because he first loved us.
note: Our love is always a reply — He said it first, and we're just answering back.

label: Sunday School
prompt: Now the serpent was more _____ than any beast of the field which the LORD God had made. And he said unto the woman, Yea, hath God said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden?
verse: Now the serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field which the LORD God had made. And he said unto the woman, Yea, hath God said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden?
note: The KJV spells it 'subtil' — and the serpent opens Eden's first conversation by questioning what God really said.

label: Deep Water
prompt: Thou art of _____ eyes than to behold evil, and canst not look on iniquity: wherefore lookest thou upon them that deal treacherously, and holdest thy tongue when the wicked devoureth the man that is more righteous than he?
verse: Thou art of purer eyes than to behold evil, and canst not look on iniquity: wherefore lookest thou upon them that deal treacherously, and holdest thy tongue when the wicked devoureth the man that is more righteous than he?
note: Habakkuk's honest complaint: if God can't bear to look on evil, why let wicked Babylon swallow people better than itself?

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall _____ unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh.
verse: Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh.
note: To 'cleave' is to stick fast — the Bible's first wedding sermon, later quoted by both Jesus and Paul.
